title: Prefill backpressure regulator and fragment restitch for paged attention cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Improve stability and tail latency of decode by introducing a prefill backpressure regulator and a fragment restitching step to reduce KV cache fragmentation during high-concurrency prefills. This ticket designs, implements, and verifies a coordinated mechanism: (1) a token-rate-aware admission controller that smooths prefill load across decode waves, (2) a fragment restitcher that merges recently-evicted adjacent fragments before reallocation, and (3) kernel co-placement hints to reduce cross-shard migrations for hot fragments.
background: We observe latency spikes when many concurrent long-prefill requests cause thrashing in the paged KV cache. Eviction churn fragments long-lived attention state; subsequent prefills suffer additional overhead as the runtime reassembles fragments and schedules kernels across multiple shards. Existing LRU-like eviction policies are reactive and do not coordinate with prefill scheduling or kernel placement, leading to increased decode stalls and higher p99 latency on multi-tenant nodes.
proposed_solution:
Three coordinated pieces:
1) Prefill Backpressure Regulator: admission control that monitors per-node token ingestion rate, reservation tokens per request, and the fraction of pages in transient (recently-evicted) state. It delays or staggers non-critical prefill work by issuing 'prefill windows' and throttling oversized batches. Regulator policy is parameterized (window_ms, max_tokens_window, burst_multiplier).
2) Fragment Restitcher: background job that identifies adjacent free fragments and recently evicted neighbor fragments and merges them into larger contiguous segments before allocating new prefill state. Uses a cheap scan limited to recent eviction buckets and honors tenant quotas.
3) Kernel Co-placement Hints: when restitcher produces a larger contiguous allocation, the allocator emits metadata so the kernel scheduler can co-place decode kernels to minimize cross-shard KV access. We add a simple affinity tag to the allocation descriptor consumed by the kernel selection layer.
These three components aim to reduce allocation churn, lower cross-shard coordination, and smooth prefill spikes without changing consumer-visible APIs.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Throttling prefills can increase median latency for some workloads; circuit-breaker thresholds must be conservative.
- Restitcher introduces background CPU/GPU memory compaction activity; must be bounded to avoid impacting decode paths.
- Affinity hints are best-effort; incorrect placement may reduce throughput for other tenants.
- Complexity of cross-component coordination increases surface area for bugs; heavy integration testing required.
implementation_notes:
- Add PrefillRegulator service in serving runtime component with metrics exposed: regulator.window_ms, tokens_allowed, tokens_used, delayed_requests_count.
- Extend allocation metadata: add fields 'affinity_tag' and 'restitch_score' (integers represented as strings in this ticket JSON).
- Implement Restitcher as periodic work item limited by budget_ms per cycle (default 10ms). It will operate on recent_eviction_buckets and merge only contiguous fragments owned by same tenant and model variant.
- Kernel scheduler: add affinity-aware placement pass that prefers GPU-local kernels when affinity_tag matches existing allocations.
- Feature flag: runtime.feature.prefill_regulator = off by default.
- Telemetry: add dashboard 'Prefill Regulator: tokens, delays, fragment merges' and alert when delayed_requests_count > 1000/5m or restitch_cpu_ms > 50ms/min.
performance_goals:
- Reduce p99 decode latency under 95th percentile concurrency by 20% in staged workloads.
- Reduce average per-request fragment reassembly overhead by 35% (measured in microseconds per prefill).
- Keep median latency within 3% of baseline for single-tenant steady-state traffic.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for regulator policy math, restitching merge correctness, and affinity tag propagation.
2) Integration tests in runtime CI that spin up multi-tenant node simulator and replay traces with synthetic long-prefill sessions to assert reduced eviction churn and stable decode latency.
3) Chaos test: schedule bursts of prefill requests across tenants and verify that regulator prevents node thrash and that restitcher reduces fragment counts.
4) Canary rollout to dedicated pool with 5% traffic and perf dashboard monitoring for 72 hours.
acceptance_criteria:
- Feature flag can be toggled at runtime without restarting nodes.
- Canary metrics show >= 15% reduction in p99 tail vs baseline under identical synthetic load, and no regression in median latency.
- Unit and integration tests pass in CI with >=95% coverage for changed modules.
- Operational dashboards display regulator and restitcher metrics; runbooks updated.
notes: Initial microbenchmarks (2025-02-20) show restitch merges reduced fragment count by ~28% on synthetic traces.
Regulator default params chosen conservatively: window_ms=100, max_tokens_window=20000, burst_multiplier=1.5
